capabilities: Encrypt secret blocks between %%secret-start%%/%%secret-end%% markers automatically on file save
Encrypt binary files (PDF, images, audio) in place and decrypt them in memory on open
Manage multi-key access so different AWS IAM users or teams can decrypt only their blocks
Re-encrypt an entire vault with a new KMS key via the ocke-rekey CLI
Show a KMS connection status indicator and warn when encryption on save is unavailable
disambiguation: Not a sync or backup tool; it only encrypts note blocks and files at rest using AWS KMS.
extras: Warns that monkey-patching the vault adapter may conflict with other plugins that modify file I/O; recommends a pre-commit Git hook to catch unencrypted plaintext; provides CLI decryption tools and an SLSA-provenance/SBOM release verification process; requires Obsidian desktop >= 1.4.0.
intentEvidence: Cloud KMS Encryption — team knowledge bases with IAM access control, DevOps secrets in Obsidian
motivation: The author wanted a Zero Trust Storage model for vaults kept in remote storage, where only ciphertext exists on disk and decryption happens locally in memory.
problem: Vault contents stored in remote storage such as S3 or Git are readable by anyone who gains access to that storage.

relations.evidence: transparent encryption of secret blocks and binary files using AWS KMS
Meld Encrypt — personal password-protected notes, single-user
SOPS — CI/CD secrets in YAML/JSON files, GitOps workflows
git-crypt — whole-file encryption in Git repos, developer workflows
This is the same approach used by gpgCrypt

summary: Envelope-encryption plugin that transparently encrypts secret blocks in notes and binary files with AWS KMS, keeping no plaintext on disk.
